headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because RD-Agent can egress broadly and use APIs while Taipy is a local, no-egress data-engineering layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and handle files/logs, so if Taipy is used as a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge, malicious content could influence RD-Agent. Taipy itself shows no ingestion or parsing surface, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and not default. Uncertainty about undocumented bridging keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Taipy is used to store content that RD-Agent later reads as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF operators manually copy Taipy-generated text into RD-Agent prompts, prompt injection can occur.
mitigations: Keep Taipy outputs in a separate folder from RD-Agent inputs.
Require manual review before pasting Taipy text into RD-Agent.
Add a prompt delimiter template for any copied content.
Use read-only exports from Taipy for RD-Agent consumption.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and can send data to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs; Taipy has no egress, so the main leakage risk is RD-Agent exporting sensitive workspace data while Taipy presents or stores it locally. The pair shares no documented isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF RD-Agent is pointed at sensitive reports or datasets, those contents may leave the environment via external APIs.
IF Taipy displays or stages the same files RD-Agent reads, sensitive data can be exposed in both tools.
mitigations: Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
Block outbound API keys except in approved runs.
Store Taipy and RD-Agent artifacts in separate directories.
Review logs for accidental sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, while Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler tool with no explicit write or concurrency surface listed. Because Taipy lacks documented mutable-resource access here, a direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to unusual shared-state setups.
conditions: IF both tools are configured to write the same log or workspace directory, file contention can occur.
IF Taipy is extended to mutate the same shared resource RD-Agent edits, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator lock.
Keep Taipy read-only over RD-Agent outputs.
Check for duplicate file targets before runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs and logs, and Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler layer that may consume those outputs. If Taipy treats RD-Agent results as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into downstream workflows. Taipy's lack of documented verification controls here makes the safer choice medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests RD-Agent-produced files without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF RD-Agent outputs are used to trigger Taipy jobs, downstream actions may amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Taipy consumes RD-Agent outputs.
Validate schemas on all exchanged files.
Use checksum checks before downstream execution.
Limit Taipy to preview mode for RD-Agent artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and approval gates.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and may send them to third-party APIs, while Taipy has no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated data classes, especially if Taipy stores or surfaces the same artifacts. The evidence is docs-only, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF financial reports or other regulated data are processed through RD-Agent APIs, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF Taipy retains or logs the same regulated artifacts, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from RD-Agent runs.
Confirm vendor DPAs before using external APIs.
Minimize retention of Taipy logs and artifacts.
Document data-class handling for both tools.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls.
